meta_description: CXMT cross-market basis, funding, and arbitrage research by Evelyn Chen.
title: CXMT Cross-Market Arbitrage & Price Discovery
subtitle: A five-minute study of Shanghai-listed CXMT, Hyperliquid's xyz:CXMT perpetual, and the funding mechanics that shape their price basis.
summary_bullets: Built an auditable five-minute data pipeline across Hyperliquid, JoinQuant, and Yahoo Finance, aligning cash and perpetual prices, time zones, and currency conversion.
Derived a basis mean-reversion hypothesis from HIP-3 oracle and funding mechanics, including the post-close decay of the oracle premium.
Backtested a cost-aware long-equity / short-perpetual strategy with T+1 restrictions, funding, execution costs, and out-of-sample monitoring.
data_title: A synchronized five-minute panel across three venues

data_rows.content: USD/CNH conversion for a common CNY price
CNY-adjusted perpetual price, basis, funding carry, and costs

data_note: The initial research window ran from July 27 to August 17, 2026. Observations after August 17 are treated as out of sample.
basis_chart_caption: Actual aligned closes from the workbook. Hover for bar-level values or use the range buttons to isolate the research window and out-of-sample period. Equal-width trading bars remove overnight gaps; lines break between trading days. Source: Hyperliquid, JoinQuant, and Yahoo Finance USD/CNH.
basis_explanation: The perpetual and the A-share trade under different hours, settlement rules, and access constraints. The HIP-3 oracle links the two venues, but T+1 execution, limited shorting, funding, and fragmented liquidity prevent immediate convergence.
funding_explanation: xyz:CXMT is a HIP-3 builder-deployed perpetual operated by trade.xyz. Its oracle carries the external reference price on-chain and updates roughly every three seconds.
funding_note: After the A-share closes, the external anchor disappears. An EWMA pulls the oracle toward the executable market range; once IPD reaches zero, premium and funding also approach zero.

strategy_title: Trade an unusually rich perpetual, then wait for the basis to normalize

strategy_steps.label: 1 · Signal
strategy_steps.detail: Z-score the log basis against the previous 72 five-minute bars—about six hours of observed trading. Shift the rolling mean and volatility by one bar.

strategy_steps.label: 2 · Enter
strategy_steps.detail: At 1.2 ≤ Z < 3 and funding ≥ −0.05% per hour, buy the A-share and short equal-notional CXMT at the next bar's open.

strategy_steps.label: 3 · Hold
strategy_steps.detail: Under T+1, do not exit on the entry day. Carry both legs across sessions while waiting for the spread to mean-revert.

strategy_steps.label: 4 · Exit
strategy_steps.detail: Exit when Z ≤ 0; stop when Z ≥ 3. Net return includes realized funding and 20 bps per completed pair trade.

intraday_note: The signal was highly profitable in the study, but mainland equity T+1 and short-sale limits make the assumed intraday execution impractical.
interday_rule: Apply the causal 72-bar signal to an equal-notional long A-share / short CXMT pair; execute on the next bar and allow overnight holding under T+1.

continuation_rows.meaning: Relative-value trading captured repeated convergence over a 4.42-year backtest; one trade remained open at −2.65%.
Rotation preserved substantially more capital than holding the A-share (−53.19%) or H-share (−57.32%), but did not produce a positive return.

footer_text: For research and educational purposes only. Backtests are not evidence of future performance.
